sources.entry: C++: _Build your own VR headset for $200_

summary.one_liner: Relativty is an open-source, build-it-yourself VR headset (hardware, firmware and SteamVR driver) that the README presents as a build guide rather than a consumer product.
summary.what_it_does: The repository documents how to build a 3-DoF VR headset from an ATmega32U4 board (such as an Arduino Pro Micro) with an IMU read through the FastIMU library, paired with a small high-refresh PC display. The Arduino firmware sends IMU readings over USB to a SteamVR driver, which is copied into the SteamVR drivers directory and configured through a default.vrsettings JSON file. That file holds the USB VID/PID, the display origin and resolution, distortion and IPD values. The README also describes a legacy build using a custom Relativty PCB or an Arduino Due with an MPU-6050 or MPU-9250, plus an experimental webcam-based body-tracking option that needs an NVIDIA GPU and CUDA. Mechanical parts are 3D-printable STL files, with lens and strap specs (40mm diameter, 50mm focal length lenses) and suggested sourcing.
use_cases: Build a low-cost DIY VR headset
Use an Arduino as a VR head tracker for SteamVR
Configure a SteamVR driver for a custom HMD display
Learn VR hardware and firmware from a build guide
Experiment with webcam-based body tracking for VR
how_to_run: Wire the IMU to the MCU (VCC, GND, SDA, SCL) and connect the MCU to the PC over USB
Install the Arduino IDE and the FastIMU library, then upload the Examples/Fastimu/Calibrated_relativty sketch
Optionally run the FastIMU calibration from the Arduino Serial Monitor
Download the repository and copy Relativty_Driver\Relativty into the SteamVR drivers directory
Edit drivers\Relativty\resources\settings\default.vrsettings with your MCU's PID/VID and display window and resolution settings
notable: Open-source hardware, firmware and SteamVR driver, with a build guide instead of a finished product
Targets 2K dual-screen output at 120 FPS, per the README
Recommended build uses an Arduino Pro Micro and a FastIMU-supported IMU
Includes a display-coordinate guide for multi-monitor setups on Windows
Experimental webcam-based 3D body tracking via a neural network
caveats: 3-DoF only, with no built-in controller support; the README points to HadesVR for 6-DoF and controllers
Display origin and resolution must be set correctly or the driver crashes and SteamVR shows nothing
Body tracking requires an NVIDIA GPU with CUDA and older PyTorch/CUDA versions, and is described as very experimental
